summary: India localization for Business Central 29 adds GST (including cess, reverse charge, advance payments, input service distribution, reconciliation, settlement), TDS and TCS, e-invoice and e-way bill, voucher interface, gate entry, subcontracting, FA depreciation and stale cheques. Use it for questions on Indian tax setup, posting and local reports.
overview:
The India layer is almost entirely additive: about 1,260 own objects (codeunits, pages, page and table extensions, enums, queries, reports) and no changes to W1 objects. GST is the largest block. Codeunits such as "GST Base Validation", "GST Posting Management", "GST Settlement" and "e-Invoice Management" sit on a tax engine, with use-case, tax type and dataset codeunits for GST, Cess, GST TDS/TCS, TDS and TCS. GST fields and pages extend the sales, purchase, service, inventory, pricing, project and setup objects.

Beyond tax, the layer adds a voucher interface with narration and books reports (Day Book, Bank Book, Cash Book, Ledger, Voucher Register), gate entry tracking, subcontracting with delivery challans and GST liability, fixed asset block and shift depreciation, charge groups, and stale cheque handling.

Microsoft Learn documents these features page by page: GST setup, purchase and sales scenarios, advance payments, settlement, reconciliation, e-invoice, e-way bill, TDS and TCS setup and payment, gate entry, voucher interface, depreciation and subcontracting.
key_points: GST engine: setup, HSN/SAC and GST groups, posting by state and component, reverse charge, exempted, composite, SEZ, import and export scenarios
GST Compensation Cess with five calculation types
GST settlement, credit adjustment journal, liability adjustment for open reverse charge invoices, input service distribution and GSTR-2A reconciliation
E-invoice (JSON, IRN, cancellation) and e-way bill Excel template export
TDS and TCS setup, calculation and payment to authorities, plus GST TCS/TDS on payments
Voucher interface with six voucher types, narration and Day Book, Bank Book, Cash Book, Ledger and Voucher Register reports
Inward and outward gate entries linked to purchase, sales, transfer and return documents
Subcontracting with delivery challans and GST liability, FA block/shift depreciation, and stale cheque setup

areas.what: Holds the core of the India layer: GST codeunits for validation, posting, settlement, journals, distribution, reconciliation, applications and reverse transactions, plus cess, TDS and TCS tax engine setup and use-case data. Also includes e-invoice management and JSON handlers, bank charge GST and non-availment logic.
areas.why: Learn pages describe GST setup, settlement, cess, e-invoice, TDS, TCS and audit trail requirements that these objects implement.

areas.what: Page extensions add GST fields to customers, sales documents and subforms, archives, statistics, finance charge memos and ledger entries. Sales posting uses GST validation and number series codeunits.
areas.why: Learn covers GST on sales to registered and unregistered customers, exports, exempted sales and sales returns.

areas.what: Page extensions add GST fields to vendors and purchase documents, archives and statistics, including charge assignment variants for purchase documents. Supports vendor types such as registered, unregistered, import, SEZ, composite and exempted.
areas.why: Learn describes GST credit, reverse charge, import and return scenarios for purchases.

areas.what: Adds gate entry tracking: inward and outward gate entries, posted gate entries, comments, attachments, a posting codeunit, enums for source type and status, and the Gate Entry report. Extends warehouse receipt pages.
areas.why: Learn explains gate entry as a record of goods entering and leaving premises, linked to purchase, sales and transfer documents.

areas.what: Provides the voucher interface (voucher posting setup, debit and credit accounts, posted narration), India books reports (Day Book, Bank Book, Cash Book, Ledger, Voucher Register), and an extended Check Report with stale cheque support. Bank account pages carry GST fields.
areas.why: Learn describes six voucher types routed by account type and a stale check feature that invalidates cheques after a set period.

areas.what: Adds income tax depreciation with FA blocks, shifts, additional depreciation, a separate accounting period for income tax, and a fiscal year close. Includes Calculate FA Depreciation and Create FA Fiscal Year reports and extensions of depreciation books.
areas.why: Learn documents block-based and shift-based depreciation setup and calculation for India.

areas.what: Table and page extensions add GST to service orders, quotes, invoices, credit memos, contracts, shipments and archives, with GST on service lines and setup.
areas.why: Learn covers GST on service orders, invoices and credit memos.

areas.what: Extends item, item charge, location, inventory setup and item template with GST fields, adds gate entry setup on inventory and transfer order pages, and adds subcontracting fields on item journal and ledger entries.
Extends company information, shipping agents and source code setup with GST, TCS, TDS and voucher-related fields.
Codeunits that import tax use cases for GST, TDS and TCS into the tax engine.
Subcontracting fields are added to production order lines and components, with a page extension on the production order line.
areas.why: Learn describes subcontracting setup with delivery challans and job work.

areas.what: Adds GST-related fields to price list lines and price worksheet lines.
Adds GST fields to the resource table and resource card.
Provides a QR Generator codeunit and a .NET reference, used for QR codes such as on e-invoices.
Permission set extension giving the D365 BASIC set access to India TDS objects.

issues: The overview says the layer is 'almost entirely additive', but the input shows it is fully additive: all 1,262 objects are its own and no W1 objects are changed. 'Additive' alone would be more precise.

The overview says use-case, tax type and dataset codeunits exist for TDS and TCS. The input only shows 'Import TDS Use Case' and 'Import TCS Use Case' for those two. Tax type and dataset codeunits are listed only for GST, Cess and GST TDS/TCS. The claim is slightly broader than the evidence.

Some documented areas are left out: audit trail and edit logs, service transfer, GST on bank charges, and charge assignment (only briefly mentioned as charge groups). They could be added if there is room, but leaving them out does not make anything wrong.
